faq.a: Yes. Gumroad lets you pay what you want, starting at $0. If it helps and you want to leave something, you can. You do not have to.
The printable is a cover and two working pages, so reading it is quick. Setting up the two automatic transfers is a one-time job at your bank.

faq.q: What if I have credit-card debt?
faq.a: The tool covers it. If you carry debt above about 7% APR, build the one-month starter buffer first, then attack the debt, then return to the full emergency fund.

faq.q: Does it only work for US accounts?
faq.a: The printable names US accounts such as a 401(k) and a Roth IRA, and the contribution limits change each year. The idea of working in a fixed order still applies elsewhere, using your own equivalents.

faq.q: Can I print it or use it on a tablet?
faq.a: Both. Print the PDF, or fill it in on a tablet with any PDF app. The Google Sheet works in your browser.
No. It is a planning tool and general education only. For decisions about taxes or your own situation, speak to a qualified adviser.
